title: Adoption mode: a new top-level osf.toml key
summary: Adds an `adoption_mode` key to a repository's own `osf.toml`, describing how osf is placed in the adopter's organisation (decision 0006). `config::adoption_mode` reads the key and returns `None` when the file or key is absent; `config::require_adoption_mode` lets a command declare which modes it supports and refuses to run on an unset or unsupported one. The layered config loader now validates the key before stripping it, so an unsupported value stops every command that loads the config, not just the ones that ask for a mode. Only one mode exists so far, `private-factory-repo`; no command depends on it yet.

nodes.subtitle: &toml::Value -> Option<AdoptionMode>
nodes.summary: Checks the key on an already-parsed osf.toml. Shared by the standalone reader and the layered loader so both reject the same values with the same message.

nodes.label: require_adoption_mode()
nodes.subtitle: root, command, supported -> AdoptionMode
nodes.summary: The gate a mode-dependent command calls: reads the key and checks it against the modes the command supports. An unset key is refused too, so a command never runs on a guessed mode. No command calls it yet.

nodes.label: config::load()
nodes.subtitle: layered osf.toml merge
nodes.summary: The layered loader now calls adoption_mode_of before stripping the key, so an unsupported value stops every command that loads config. The key is then removed from the table so it never trips deny_unknown_fields.
